spec.description: NASA FIRMS's satellite fire detections (VIIRS, the last week) against the high-voltage grid of OpenStreetMap, in one of four regions: how far every fire fell from the nearest line of 200 kV or more, which lines and how many kilometres of them a fire came within reach of, played pass by pass. Distances are measured on the server in an equal-area projection; the week then loads into your browser, where a timeline, Mosaic histograms and filters cross-filter the map, the cards and the table with DuckDB-WASM. Data: NASA FIRMS, OpenStreetMap contributors via Overture Maps (ODbL).
VIIRS detections the filters keep. One detection is a 375 m pixel flagged hot on one pass: a fire seen on three passes counts three times.
spec.title: Fire detections

options.spec:
params:
  fireFilters: { select: crossfilter }
plot:
  - mark: text
    data: { from: fires, filterBy: $fireFilters }
    text: { count: }
    frameAnchor: middle
    fill: currentColor
    fontSize: 40
    fontWeight: 500
xAxis: null
yAxis: null
margin: 0

options.content:
**Fires.** [NASA FIRMS](https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/) active fire detections from the VIIRS instrument on
Suomi NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 (collection 2, 375 m), the last seven days of the region's file, read through the
gateway, which caches them. A detection is one pixel flagged as hot on one pass, not a fire's outline: a fire burning
for days counts again on every pass. **Fire radiative power** (FRP, MW) is the rate at which the pixel radiates heat.
Confidence is FIRMS's own (low, nominal, high); low-confidence pixels include sun glint and hot surfaces.

**The grid.** Overhead lines and cables of 200 kV and more from [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright)
(ODbL), as the base theme of an [Overture Maps](https://overturemaps.org/) release carries them, with the voltage,
name and operator tagged on the way. Each instance builds the file once with `datasets/power-grid/build.sh`. A line is
an OSM way: long circuits are several ways, so "lines reached" counts sections. Mapping is uneven: where a line is
missing, the fires near it read as far from the grid.

**Distances** are measured on the server in an equal-area projection of the region (Albers for South America,
Africa, Australia and California) with DuckDB's `spatial` extension: to the nearest line for every detection (up to 50 km),
and to every line within the chosen distance for the stretches and the table. The stretch a fire reaches is the part of
the line within that distance of it; a line's km reached joins the stretches of all the fires the filters keep, so
overlaps count once.

**In your browser.** The three tables (grid, detections, detection-line pairs) load once per region into DuckDB-WASM
(Chaski); the timeline, the histograms, the filters and the map's GPU filter cross-filter them through one Mosaic
selection, with no further request to the server. Changing *Near means within* reloads the pairs.

spec.description: Every filter of the dashboard, each counting what the others leave: distance to the nearest line, fire radiative power, the voltage of the nearest line, day or night, satellite, confidence and an area drawn on the map. Brush a histogram or pick values; × clears one filter, Clear all every one.
spec.title: Filters

spec.rawSql:
WITH iv AS (
  SELECT line_id, a_km AS a, b_km AS b FROM $pairs WHERE $__crossfilter($pairFilters)
),
o AS (
  SELECT *, max(b) OVER (PARTITION BY line_id ORDER BY a, b ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS seen
  FROM iv
),
runs AS (
  SELECT *, sum(CASE WHEN seen IS NULL OR a > seen THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
              OVER (PARTITION BY line_id ORDER BY a, b ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS run
  FROM o
),
reached AS (
  SELECT line_id, sum(len) AS km FROM (SELECT line_id, run, max(b) - min(a) AS len FROM runs GROUP BY ALL) GROUP BY line_id
)
SELECT round(sum(km))::DOUBLE AS km FROM reached

spec.rawSql:
-- Every detection of the week, once: time, distance, power, satellite, day or
-- night, confidence and voltage are filtered in the map, on the GPU, where the
-- clauses of the fireFilters selection land.
SELECT time, latitude, longitude, frp, frp_log, satellite, daynight, confidence, line_km, band, voltage
FROM $fires
SELECT id, name, operator, kv, voltage, kind, km, geom FROM $grid

-- The stretches of line within the chosen distance of a fire, one per line and
-- kilometre along it, where the filters keep at least one detection.
WITH kept AS (
  SELECT line_id, cell, count(*)::DOUBLE AS detections, min(fire_km) AS fire_km, max(frp) AS frp,
         max(time) AS last_seen
  FROM $pairs
  WHERE $__crossfilter($pairFilters)
  GROUP BY line_id, cell
)
SELECT p.line_id, p.line AS name, p.operator, p.kv, k.detections, k.fire_km, k.frp, k.last_seen, p.geom
FROM $pairs AS p
JOIN kept AS k ON k.line_id = p.line_id AND k.cell = p.cell
WHERE p.geom IS NOT NULL

spec.rawSql:
WITH iv AS (
  SELECT line_id, a_km AS a, b_km AS b FROM $pairs WHERE $__crossfilter($pairFilters)
),
o AS (
  SELECT *, max(b) OVER (PARTITION BY line_id ORDER BY a, b ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS seen
  FROM iv
),
runs AS (
  SELECT *, sum(CASE WHEN seen IS NULL OR a > seen THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
              OVER (PARTITION BY line_id ORDER BY a, b ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS run
  FROM o
),
reached AS (
  SELECT line_id, sum(len) AS km FROM (SELECT line_id, run, max(b) - min(a) AS len FROM runs GROUP BY ALL) GROUP BY line_id
)
SELECT any_value(p.line) AS "Line", any_value(p.osm_way) AS osm_way, any_value(p.operator) AS "Operator",
       any_value(p.kv) AS "kV", count(*)::DOUBLE AS "Near", round(any_value(x.km), 1) AS "Km reached",
       any_value(p.line_length_km) AS "Length, km", min(p.fire_km) AS "Closest, km",
       round(max(p.frp)) AS "Max MW", max(p.time) AS "Last seen"
FROM $pairs AS p
JOIN reached AS x USING (line_id)
WHERE $__crossfilter($pairFilters)
GROUP BY p.line_id
ORDER BY "Near" DESC, "Closest, km"
LIMIT 100

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: the high-voltage grid of the region, once per region, for the map.
-- Geometry simplified to about 200 m.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT * FROM (VALUES
      ('central-brazil', 'South_America', 'ESRI:102033', -25, -60, -2, -38, -13.5, -49),
      ('southern-africa', 'Southern_Africa', 'ESRI:102022', -22, 12, -5, 42, -13.5, 27),
      ('eastern-australia', 'Australia_NewZealand', 'EPSG:3577', -39, 138, -10, 154, -24.5, 146),
      ('california', 'USA_contiguous_and_Hawaii', 'EPSG:3310', 32.5, -124.5, 42, -114, 37.2, -119.3)
  ) v(region, firms, crs, s, w, n, e, lat, lng)
  WHERE region = ${region:sqlstring}
),
-- The lines of 200 kV and more, built once per instance from Overture
-- Maps (the power lines of OpenStreetMap) by datasets/power-grid/build.sh, measured
-- in an equal-area projection of the region.
grid AS (
  SELECT l.id, l.osm_way, l.name, l.operator, l.kv, l.kind, l.km, l.geometry AS geom,
         CASE WHEN l.kv >= 600 THEN '600 kV and more' WHEN l.kv >= 400 THEN '400-599 kV'
              WHEN l.kv >= 300 THEN '300-399 kV' ELSE '200-299 kV' END AS voltage,
         ST_Transform(l.geometry, 'EPSG:4326', r.crs, always_xy := true) AS xy
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/power-grid/lines.parquet') AS l, r
  WHERE l.xmax >= r.w AND l.xmin <= r.e AND l.ymax >= r.s AND l.ymin <= r.n
)
SELECT id, name, operator, kv, voltage, kind, km,
       ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology(geom, 0.002))::VARCHAR AS geom
FROM grid

spec.description: The week of detections in the region with their distance to the grid, loaded into the browser once per region.
spec.name: fires

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: one row per detection, with its distance to the nearest line of
-- the grid, measured in an equal-area projection of the region up to 50 km (50
-- stands for 50 km or more). Loaded once per region: the timeline, the
-- histograms and the map filter it in your browser.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT * FROM (VALUES
      ('central-brazil', 'South_America', 'ESRI:102033', -25, -60, -2, -38, -13.5, -49),
      ('southern-africa', 'Southern_Africa', 'ESRI:102022', -22, 12, -5, 42, -13.5, 27),
      ('eastern-australia', 'Australia_NewZealand', 'EPSG:3577', -39, 138, -10, 154, -24.5, 146),
      ('california', 'USA_contiguous_and_Hawaii', 'EPSG:3310', 32.5, -124.5, 42, -114, 37.2, -119.3)
  ) v(region, firms, crs, s, w, n, e, lat, lng)
  WHERE region = ${region:sqlstring}
),
-- The lines of 200 kV and more, built once per instance from Overture
-- Maps (the power lines of OpenStreetMap) by datasets/power-grid/build.sh, measured
-- in an equal-area projection of the region.
grid AS (
  SELECT l.id, l.osm_way, l.name, l.operator, l.kv, l.kind, l.km, l.geometry AS geom,
         CASE WHEN l.kv >= 600 THEN '600 kV and more' WHEN l.kv >= 400 THEN '400-599 kV'
              WHEN l.kv >= 300 THEN '300-399 kV' ELSE '200-299 kV' END AS voltage,
         ST_Transform(l.geometry, 'EPSG:4326', r.crs, always_xy := true) AS xy
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/power-grid/lines.parquet') AS l, r
  WHERE l.xmax >= r.w AND l.xmin <= r.e AND l.ymax >= r.s AND l.ymin <= r.n
),
-- Every VIIRS detection of the last seven days in the region, from the three
-- satellites, as FIRMS publishes them (through the gateway, cached).
fires AS (
  SELECT row_number() OVER () AS fire,
         strptime(acq_date::VARCHAR || lpad(acq_time::VARCHAR, 4, '0'), '%Y-%m-%d%H%M') AS time,
         latitude, longitude, frp, satellite, daynight, confidence::VARCHAR AS confidence,
         ST_Transform(ST_Point(longitude, latitude), 'EPSG:4326', r.crs, always_xy := true) AS xy
  FROM read_csv(['http://feeds/firms/noaa-20-viirs-c2/J1_VIIRS_C2_${firms:raw}_7d.csv',
                 'http://feeds/firms/noaa-21-viirs-c2/J2_VIIRS_C2_${firms:raw}_7d.csv',
                 'http://feeds/firms/suomi-npp-viirs-c2/SUOMI_VIIRS_C2_${firms:raw}_7d.csv'], union_by_name = true), r
  WHERE latitude BETWEEN r.s AND r.n AND longitude BETWEEN r.w AND r.e
),
nearest AS (
  SELECT f.fire, arg_min(g.id, ST_Distance(f.xy, g.xy)) AS line_id, min(ST_Distance(f.xy, g.xy)) / 1000 AS km
  FROM fires AS f JOIN grid AS g ON ST_DWithin(f.xy, g.xy, 50000)
  GROUP BY f.fire
)
SELECT f.time, f.latitude, f.longitude, round(f.frp, 1) AS frp,
       round(log10(greatest(f.frp, 0.1)), 3) AS frp_log,
       CASE f.satellite WHEN 'N' THEN 'Suomi NPP' WHEN 'N20' THEN 'NOAA-20' WHEN 'N21' THEN 'NOAA-21'
                        ELSE f.satellite END AS satellite,
       CASE f.daynight WHEN 'N' THEN 'Night' ELSE 'Day' END AS daynight,
       f.confidence,
       round(least(coalesce(n.km, 50), 50), 2) AS line_km,
       CASE WHEN coalesce(n.km, 50) < 1 THEN 'under 1 km' WHEN coalesce(n.km, 50) < 2 THEN '1-2 km' WHEN coalesce(n.km, 50) < 5 THEN '2-5 km'
            WHEN coalesce(n.km, 50) < 10 THEN '5-10 km' WHEN coalesce(n.km, 50) < 20 THEN '10-20 km' ELSE '20 km or more' END AS band,
       coalesce(g.voltage, 'none within 50 km') AS voltage
FROM fires AS f
LEFT JOIN nearest AS n USING (fire)
LEFT JOIN grid AS g ON g.id = n.line_id
ORDER BY f.time

spec.description: The detections within 20 km of a line, for the distance charts: a copy of part of fires, in the browser.
spec.name: near

source.sql:
-- The detections within 20 km of a line, for the two distance charts: without
-- the far ones (most of them), their bars keep a readable scale. Brushing them
-- filters fires too: the Mosaic selection cuts any table with the column.
SELECT * FROM $fires WHERE line_km < 20

spec.description: Each detection and line within the chosen distance of each other, loaded into the browser once per region and distance.
spec.name: pairs

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: one row per detection and line within the chosen distance
-- (${km} km) of each other: a fire between two lines counts for both. a_km and
-- b_km bound the stretch of line within that distance of the fire, as
-- kilometres along the line; the browser joins the stretches of a line to
-- measure how much of it was reached. cell is the kilometre of line the fire
-- faces, and one row per cell carries geom, the stretch that the fires of the
-- cell reach together, for the map. line_km, band and the fire columns repeat
-- those of fires, so the same filters cut both.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT * FROM (VALUES
      ('central-brazil', 'South_America', 'ESRI:102033', -25, -60, -2, -38, -13.5, -49),
      ('southern-africa', 'Southern_Africa', 'ESRI:102022', -22, 12, -5, 42, -13.5, 27),
      ('eastern-australia', 'Australia_NewZealand', 'EPSG:3577', -39, 138, -10, 154, -24.5, 146),
      ('california', 'USA_contiguous_and_Hawaii', 'EPSG:3310', 32.5, -124.5, 42, -114, 37.2, -119.3)
  ) v(region, firms, crs, s, w, n, e, lat, lng)
  WHERE region = ${region:sqlstring}
),
-- The lines of 200 kV and more, built once per instance from Overture
-- Maps (the power lines of OpenStreetMap) by datasets/power-grid/build.sh, measured
-- in an equal-area projection of the region.
grid AS (
  SELECT l.id, l.osm_way, l.name, l.operator, l.kv, l.kind, l.km, l.geometry AS geom,
         CASE WHEN l.kv >= 600 THEN '600 kV and more' WHEN l.kv >= 400 THEN '400-599 kV'
              WHEN l.kv >= 300 THEN '300-399 kV' ELSE '200-299 kV' END AS voltage,
         ST_Transform(l.geometry, 'EPSG:4326', r.crs, always_xy := true) AS xy
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/power-grid/lines.parquet') AS l, r
  WHERE l.xmax >= r.w AND l.xmin <= r.e AND l.ymax >= r.s AND l.ymin <= r.n
),
-- Every VIIRS detection of the last seven days in the region, from the three
-- satellites, as FIRMS publishes them (through the gateway, cached).
fires AS (
  SELECT row_number() OVER () AS fire,
         strptime(acq_date::VARCHAR || lpad(acq_time::VARCHAR, 4, '0'), '%Y-%m-%d%H%M') AS time,
         latitude, longitude, frp, satellite, daynight, confidence::VARCHAR AS confidence,
         ST_Transform(ST_Point(longitude, latitude), 'EPSG:4326', r.crs, always_xy := true) AS xy
  FROM read_csv(['http://feeds/firms/noaa-20-viirs-c2/J1_VIIRS_C2_${firms:raw}_7d.csv',
                 'http://feeds/firms/noaa-21-viirs-c2/J2_VIIRS_C2_${firms:raw}_7d.csv',
                 'http://feeds/firms/suomi-npp-viirs-c2/SUOMI_VIIRS_C2_${firms:raw}_7d.csv'], union_by_name = true), r
  WHERE latitude BETWEEN r.s AND r.n AND longitude BETWEEN r.w AND r.e
),
pairs AS (
  SELECT f.fire, g.id AS line_id, ST_Distance(f.xy, g.xy) AS d, ST_Length(g.xy) AS len,
         ST_LineLocatePoint(g.xy, f.xy) * ST_Length(g.xy) AS pos
  FROM fires AS f JOIN grid AS g ON ST_DWithin(f.xy, g.xy, ${km:raw} * 1000)
),
reach AS (
  SELECT *, min(d) OVER (PARTITION BY fire) AS nearest, floor(pos / 1000) AS cell,
         greatest(pos - sqrt(greatest(pow(${km:raw} * 1000, 2) - d * d, 0)), 0) AS a,
         least(pos + sqrt(greatest(pow(${km:raw} * 1000, 2) - d * d, 0)), len) AS b
  FROM pairs
),
cells AS (
  SELECT line_id, cell, min(fire) AS fire, min(a) AS a, max(b) AS b, any_value(len) AS len
  FROM reach GROUP BY line_id, cell
),
shapes AS (
  SELECT c.line_id, c.fire,
         ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_Transform(ST_Simplify(ST_LineSubstring(g.xy, c.a / nullif(c.len, 0), c.b / nullif(c.len, 0)), 50),
                                   r.crs, 'EPSG:4326', always_xy := true))::VARCHAR AS geom
  FROM cells AS c JOIN grid AS g ON g.id = c.line_id, r
)
SELECT f.time, f.latitude, f.longitude, round(f.frp, 1) AS frp,
       round(log10(greatest(f.frp, 0.1)), 3) AS frp_log,
       CASE f.satellite WHEN 'N' THEN 'Suomi NPP' WHEN 'N20' THEN 'NOAA-20' WHEN 'N21' THEN 'NOAA-21'
                        ELSE f.satellite END AS satellite,
       CASE f.daynight WHEN 'N' THEN 'Night' ELSE 'Day' END AS daynight,
       f.confidence,
       round(p.nearest / 1000, 2) AS line_km,
       CASE WHEN p.nearest / 1000 < 1 THEN 'under 1 km' WHEN p.nearest / 1000 < 2 THEN '1-2 km' WHEN p.nearest / 1000 < 5 THEN '2-5 km'
            WHEN p.nearest / 1000 < 10 THEN '5-10 km' WHEN p.nearest / 1000 < 20 THEN '10-20 km' ELSE '20 km or more' END AS band,
       g.voltage, p.line_id, g.osm_way, g.name AS line, g.operator, g.kv, round(p.len / 1000, 1) AS line_length_km,
       round(p.d / 1000, 2) AS fire_km, p.cell, round(p.a / 1000, 3) AS a_km, round(p.b / 1000, 3) AS b_km,
       s.geom
FROM reach AS p
JOIN fires AS f USING (fire)
JOIN grid AS g ON g.id = p.line_id
LEFT JOIN shapes AS s ON s.line_id = p.line_id AND s.fire = p.fire
ORDER BY f.time

spec.sql: SELECT DISTINCT voltage AS value FROM $fires WHERE voltage IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1
SELECT DISTINCT daynight AS value FROM $fires WHERE daynight IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1
SELECT DISTINCT satellite AS value FROM $fires WHERE satellite IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1
